item.title: Mountain village in SW China finds new path on Long March route
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
This undated photo shows a view of Jieshang Village in Gaopo Township, Guiyang, southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua) GUIYANG, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- He Zhicheng returned to his mountain village in southwest China's Guizhou Province in 2024 to open a farmhouse restaurant, after eight years on the Foxconn assembly line in Zhengzhou, capital of central China's Henan Province -- some 1,500 kilometers away. "When I worked away from home, I barely got to see my family," He said. "Now, I drop my eldest daughter off at school every morning, and revolve my days around the restaurant, looking after my younger daughter while serving guests." His return is hardly unique in his native Jieshang Village. The community is now drawing more young people back home by tapping into its historical heritage -- revolutionary sites linked to the Red Army's Long March, the epic 1934-1936 trek that broke through Kuomintang siege -- and advancing rural development. In April 1935, the Red Army made a stopover in Jieshang to rest and regroup during the Long March, forging close ties with local residents. Today, the village still preserves the slogans the soldiers painted, the billets where they stayed, and the grave of civilians who supported them. The village, however, had long struggled to develop, hindered by its remote, mountainous location and scattered farmland. "Collective revenue was meager, and we had no signature industry," recalled Yang Lun, the village Party secretary. The year 2023 marked a major turning point, as Jieshang was selected as a pilot village for a national program to develop "beautiful and revolutionary" rural communities, thereby securing both policy support and funding. A centerpiece initiative of the program was the construction of a 2.5-kilometer trail retracing the Long March route. Within the village, the trail passes through more than 100 household plots. "In rural China, villagers don't easily part with their land -- not an inch," said Yan Jiayun, the first Party secretary stationed in Jieshang. "But we told them: if no one comes (into the program), what you grow will remain yours, and yours alone -- it will never bring about more returns." First Party secretaries are designated officials sent by higher-level governments to live in villages and assist with local development. By 2025, more than 3 million such officials had been dispatched nationwide, helping to improve rural infrastructure, boost collective economies, and upgrade public services by introducing projects and coordinating resources. To get the project off the ground, Jieshang village officials formed a task force, led the way by offering their own land, and went door-to-door to help villagers see the long-term benefits and development prospects. In the end, 110 households agreed to give up their land -- free of charge -- and the trail was completed. Leveraging its restored Red Army relics and the Long March trail, Jieshang, together with a private company, set up a tourism operator in the name of the village collective. It has since integrated nearby ecological attractions, such as flower fields, camping sites, and a grassland park, into a package of themed tours. "By combining revolutionary heritage with natural scenery, we've achieved a synergy where the whole is greater than the sum of its parts," said Qiao Yingshan, a staff member at the tourism company. Since the tour program was launched, Jieshang has hosted four rural "red trail" walking events, with the largest drawing up to 700 participants. As visitors flocked to the area, many villagers began setting up roadside stands along the trail to sell locally grown specialties. "One snack stand raked in 700 to 800 yuan (about 110 U.S. dollars) in just half a day," Yan said. "When we went around to check on sales, every villager we met was beaming. That was truly heartening." The growth of "red tourism" is creating tangible job opportunities for locals. According to Yan, the village's one-day tour itinerary, launched this year, has fueled steady demand for guides, interpreters and drivers. Five farm-stay businesses, including He's family operation, have now opened in the village, employing dozens of residents. In the meantime, the tourism boom has given a new lease on life to a local red rice variety with a cultivation history of more than 600 years. Grown at an average altitude of 1,500 meters in Gaopo Township, where Jieshang is located, the rice has a long growing cycle and relatively low yields. It used to sell poorly, and villagers had little incentive to plant it. After the project got underway, Jieshang registered a company under the village collective to create the "Jieshang Hongxin" red rice brand, introducing unified purchasing, pricing and marketing. The village also brought in agricultural experts to provide technical support, which significantly boosted farmers' enthusiasm. In 2024, the village's red rice planting area reached 541 mu (about 36 hectares), and surpassed 800 mu in 2025. Zhang Quan, a villager, said he used to carry dozens of kilograms of red rice on his back to sell at the market. Now, with the village collective guaranteeing purchases at minimum prices, he grows more than 20 mu of red rice, earning about 80,000 yuan a year from the crop alone, while also running small side businesses during the off-season to supplement his income. On top of stable raw grain sales, Jieshang has further expanded its industrial chain by bringing in a business partner to produce red rice wine, boosting the added value of local agricultural products. The village has also converted idle farmhouses into a "Red Village Supermarket" to display and sell local specialties, including red rice and black pork products. Like He, Li Linghui, who runs the supermarket, is another young returnee. After working away from home for years, she had built up solid business experience. At the urging of the former village Party secretary, she invested in the village's collective company. "I wanted to do my part to help drive the village's development," Li said. "I felt it was a meaningful thing to do, so I came back." Before the rural revitalization efforts, the village's collective revenue stood at barely 200,000 yuan in 2023. It exceeded 430,000 yuan in 2024 and jumped to 570,000 yuan last year. "Our principle is to provide support without overstepping, and to assist without taking over," Yan said. The resident task force, he explained, aims to help the village build its own industries and leave behind a development model that can sustain itself over the long run. As collective revenue has grown, the village's public spaces have also undergone a quiet transformation. In recent years, Jieshang has built new facilities including a cultural square, a basketball court and a circular walking path. When night falls, the square is brightly lit. Local children gather there and sing revolutionary songs, their young, clear voices echoing through the mountains. "Every time I see this scene, I'm deeply moved," Yan said. "Isn't this exactly the legacy our revolutionary forebears wanted to leave behind?" ■ Yan Jiayun, the first Party secretary stationed in Jieshang Village, briefs college students in front of the "Red Village Supermarket" in Jieshang Village of Gaopo Township, Guiyang, southwest China's Guizhou Province, July 11, 2026. (Xinhua)

item.title: China's free final-year kindergarten policy benefits 24 mln children: ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- About 24 million children enrolled in kindergartens across China have benefited from a policy waiving childcare and education fees for the final year of preschool, a finance official said on Friday. Meanwhile, more than 25 million infants and toddlers have received childcare subsidies for 2026, said Wang Xinxiang, director of the Budget Department of the Ministry of Finance, at a press conference. China introduced a nationwide childcare subsidy program in 2025, offering an annual tax-free subsidy of 3,600 yuan (about 530 U.S. dollars) for each child under the age of three. The country also began waiving childcare and education fees for the final year of kindergarten in the 2025 autumn semester, marking another step in easing the financial burden on families with young children. These policies are among China's broader efforts to build a birth-friendly society amid declining birth rates and an aging population. ■

item.title: China pioneers AI-driven education as world seeks new schooling models
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- As classrooms worldwide grapple with the transformative yet disruptive power of artificial intelligence (AI), a fundamental question hangs over the future of education: what is schooling for when machines can outthink humans? This question has recently taken center stage in Beijing, where global academics, policymakers and frontline educators gathered to map out new models for teaching in the intelligent era. Amid the lively cross-border exchanges, one reality is clear: China's large-scale experiments with AI-driven education -- from AI plus various disciplines to AI teaching assistants -- have already put it miles ahead of most peers. At the opening ceremony of the Global Smart Education Conference 2026, Ren Youqun, China's vice minister of education and president of the Chinese National Commission for UNESCO, said that China has made the integration of AI and education a national priority. The country is pushing forward a digital education strategy that embeds intelligent technologies across all teaching elements, processes and scenarios. AI-DRIVEN EDUCATION China has rolled out an "AI Plus Education" action plan that sets out systematic arrangements for talent cultivation, application innovation, infrastructure development and ecosystem building. The plan signals a strategic pivot from pilot projects and isolated trials to system-wide deployment and full implementation. Chinese tech companies are moving quickly to translate the strategy into action. Tech giant Huawei has unveiled its AI Practice Lab (AIPL) solution for higher education, designed to cultivate interdisciplinary talent through a "multi-disciplinary plus AI" model that shifts the focus from AI knowledge acquisition to AI-driven hands-on practice, according to Zhang Chengtao, vice president of Huawei's Global Public Sector BU. In March 2026, Beijing Institute of Technology and Huawei jointly established an AIPL covering three cross-disciplinary tracks: embodied intelligence plus AI, law plus AI, and chemistry plus AI. The lab uses real-world scenarios and data to sharpen students' practical skills, Zhang said. Joining the push, another Chinese tech firm, iFLYTEK, recently introduced "Sparklight," an AI-powered super-agent designed as a one-stop assistant for teachers, covering lesson planning, student assessment, home-school communication and administrative tasks. The platform aims to free educators from repetitive paperwork and give them more time for teaching. The system adapts to individual teaching styles over time and builds up a personalized repository of teaching resources. Trial data show it boosts lesson preparation efficiency by more than 60 percent, reduces routine administrative workload by 60 percent to 80 percent, and saves each teacher four to seven hours per week for higher-value instructional activities, said Nie Xiaolin, co-founder and senior vice president of iFlytek. "Teachers are evolving from users to developers of AI applications on the Sparklight," Nie said. He cited a 3D virtual experiment for measuring bell-tower heights and an interactive 3D model of Earth's spheres as vivid examples of this shift, both created by frontline teachers using the platform. GLOBAL COOPERATION "As for the common question of our time -- 'what role should education play in the age of AI?' -- the international community must act in concert," Ren said. "We need to build strategic consensus on development, establish platforms for sharing digital education resources, and jointly enhance teachers' digital literacy and teaching competence worldwide, so as to chart a shared blueprint for the future of smart education." Chen Qun, UNESCO's assistant director-general for education, identified a host of challenges confronting global education, including demographic shifts, geopolitical tensions, underinvestment and a widening mismatch between skills training and labor market demands. Rabab Fatima, UN under-secretary-general and high representative for the least developed countries, landlocked developing countries and small island developing states, said in a video address that leveraging AI and digital technologies to advance inclusive, equitable and sustainable education is an urgent shared task for all nations. The conference unveiled the Global Smart School Initiative, an open, evidence-based platform designed to facilitate exchanges, professional assessment, transformation consulting and certification among schools worldwide. The initiative features best-practice cases from more than a dozen schools in China, the Netherlands, Serbia, Singapore, Canada and Kenya, offering reference models for digital transformation. Mo'ale 'Otunuku, minister for education and training of Tonga, stressed that AI must not become an exclusive resource for the privileged few, and that equitable access must be guaranteed. He also cautioned that educational equity entails cultural preservation, urging nations to develop localized intelligent systems that respect indigenous languages, regional civilizations and traditional knowledge systems, thereby countering the risk of cultural homogenization. ■

item.title: China urges Japan to heed insightful views from ruling, opposition parties to mend ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian on Friday called on Japanese authorities to listen to insightful views from Japan's ruling and opposition parties to repair bilateral ties. Lin made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on media reports that a cross-party group of Japanese lawmakers will visit China next week in an apparent move to help mend strained bilateral ties. "We note that some insightful figures from Japan's ruling and opposition parties are deeply concerned about the current state of China-Japan relations and hope to make efforts to put bilateral ties on the right track," Lin said. Japanese authorities should listen to and take seriously these voices, abide by all the principles set forth in the four political documents between China and Japan, and take concrete actions to create the necessary conditions for normal exchanges between the two countries, he said. ■

item.title: China considers law amendment to boost foreign-related legal services
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
BEIJING, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers are set to review a draft amendment to the lawyers law to strengthen foreign-related legal services, a spokesperson said Friday. The draft amendment seeks to improve the training of lawyers specializing in international legal affairs, Huang Haihua, spokesperson for the Legislative Affairs Commission of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, told a press conference. It also supports law firms in improving foreign-related services and encourages greater international exchanges and cooperation, Huang said. Xue Jimin, vice president of the All China Lawyers Association, said the draft amendment comes as Chinese companies and citizens face growing legal risks overseas amid a complex international environment, thus underscoring the need for more professional and internationally capable legal services. The draft is of great significance in better safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies and citizens overseas, Xue added. China's foreign-related legal services sector has expanded rapidly in recent years, with the number of lawyers providing such services growing to 12,000 and Chinese law firms setting up 207 branches in 37 countries and regions, according to a report by the Legal Daily. The draft amendment will be submitted for a second reading at a session of the NPC Standing Committee from Aug. 25 to 28. The draft also allows legal practitioners from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) and practicing lawyers from the Macao SAR who pass the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) lawyer qualification exam and obtain mainland practicing qualifications, to provide legal services within the prescribed scope in the nine mainland cities of the GBA. The draft provisions build on an existing pilot program in the GBA. In 2020, the NPC Standing Committee authorized the State Council to launch this pilot program, which was extended in 2023 to Oct. 4, 2026. Since the pilot program began, more than 600 lawyers from Hong Kong and Macao have practiced in the nine mainland cities of the GBA, providing high-quality legal services to support the region's development. Xue said the pilot program had produced positive results over nearly six years, demonstrating that the policy was successful and should now become a long-term, well-established arrangement. The draft amendment encourages and supports law firms and lawyers to participate in public-interest legal services, said Huang. It also pushes for full lawyer representation in criminal cases. The measure is expected to strengthen criminal defense and better protect human rights, said Lyu Hongbing, a veteran lawyer and national political advisor. According to the Legal Daily, relevant authorities have steadily advanced efforts to pilot full lawyer representation in criminal cases in recent years, assigning legal aid lawyers to suspects and defendants who did not hire their own lawyers due to financial difficulties and other reasons. The rate of lawyer representation in criminal cases has risen significantly, said the newspaper. Huang said that the draft amendment was open to public opinion from June 26 to July 25 and had received extensive feedback from the public and NPC deputies. Some of their suggestions are reflected in relevant provisions. ■

item.title: China ramps up policy support to unlock domestic demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-21
The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on leveraging a proactive fiscal policy to promote high-quality economic and social development in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xin) BEIJING, Aug. 21 (Xinhua) -- China will introduce a new package of policies and measures to further expand domestic demand and strengthen the momentum of economic growth, China's Vice Minister of Finance Liao Min disclosed on Friday. Speaking at a press conference, Liao said the ministry will formulate and roll out practical and effective new policy measures in a timely manner in light of macroeconomic developments in the latter half of the year. The country's fiscal policies will continue to focus on accelerating fund use, expanding domestic demand, and strengthening fiscal reform and management, the vice minister stressed. Expanding domestic demand has become increasingly important for China to sustain economic growth and strengthen its economy's resilience amid external uncertainties. Liao said China has long been the world's second-largest consumer market for goods and the largest online retail market. It is also one of the world's major import markets for consumer goods, with products from countries around the world enjoying strong popularity among Chinese consumers. As people's incomes continue to rise, consumer demand has become more diversified, Liao said. Services consumption, green consumption and new forms of consumption have emerged as bright spots, while tourism, performances and sporting events have remained popular. Products such as smartwatches and smart glasses are also widely sought after, with sales posting multifold growth. All these trends demonstrate the strong endogenous momentum of China's consumer market, Liao said. China has continued to expand domestic demand through multiple measures. So far this year, the ministry has allocated 187.5 billion yuan (about 27.65 billion U.S. dollars) to support consumer goods trade-in programs, helping generate 178 million purchases with a combined sales of approximately 1.32 trillion yuan. China has also introduced interest subsidies for personal consumption loans and loans to service-sector business entities, while supporting employment and entrepreneurship among key groups. Efforts have also been made to improve the consumption environment by advancing the development of pilot cities for modern commercial circulation systems and piloting new forms, models and scenarios of consumption. Liao said China has optimized the implementation of coordinated fiscal and financial policies to boost domestic demand, with the new measures taking effect on Aug. 1. The measures broaden the scope of interest subsidies for consumer loans. New credit-card installment purchases, including those for cars and home decoration, are now eligible for policy support. The number of financial institutions handling interest subsidies for loans to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and service-sector businesses has increased from about 100 to around 400, Liao said. The measures also raise the loan caps under the interest subsidy policy, from 50 million yuan to 75 million yuan for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, and from 10 million yuan to 20 million yuan for service-sector businesses. Liao said the interest subsidy ceiling for personal consumption loans has also been raised from 3,000 yuan to 5,000 yuan. The Ministry of Finance, in line with economic development needs, is continuing to formulate new coordinated fiscal and financial policies and measures, which will be rolled out in the second half of this year, said Liao. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Hichilema on re-election as Zambian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-20
BEIJING, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday congratulated Hakainde Hichilema on his re-election as president of Zambia. In his message, Xi said that they have met twice in recent years, and jointly steered the development of China-Zambia relations. The political mutual trust between the two countries has continued to deepen, practical cooperation has been fruitful, and China and Zambia have closely coordinated and cooperated in multilateral affairs, he said. Xi said he attaches great importance to the development of China-Zambia ties, and stands ready to work with Hichilema to implement the outcomes of the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. He also pledged to join the Zambian leader in carrying forward traditional friendship, cementing mutual support, and continuously raising the level of mutually beneficial cooperation, so as to take the China-Zambia comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. ■
